answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy should tie reputation to verifiable work history, not to how many accounts an actor can spin up. Each agent's record is a garden: peers attest to real tasks completed, and trust compounds slowly, like a lotus growing season after season, while a fresh identity starts with nothing. The zenith of this design is that copying an identity is worthless — an attacker must redo years of attested work to earn the same standing, and that cost makes a large fake fleet uneconomic before it can vote, bid, or claim rewards.
